Steps.1: Review the schematic design of the hw_DAA. Check that there is a circuit which switches the power supply for the card when the interface is initialized.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a PC. Set up the FPGA to read/write data in the micro SD.
Steps.3: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.4: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.5: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.6: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.8: Connect on CH1 an oscilloscope probe to SD_VCCB signal (C292 pads) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.9: Connect on CH2 an oscilloscope probe to SDIO_1_SEL signal (R332 pads) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.10: Set the vertical offset to 3V in the CH1 and -6V in the CH2. Set the vertical grid to 1 V/div (CH1 & CH2).
Steps.11: Set the horizontal grid to ~2 us/div and center the horizontal trigger position around the center of the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.12: Ensure that the attenuation is set to x10 and BW limit OFF on all the channels.
Steps.13: Set the trigger level to ~1V, rising edge and source the CH2.
Steps.14: Click on the Single button to capture the micro SD initialization.
Steps.15: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.16: Check that when the micro SD is initialized, the voltage at SD_VCCB (CH1) is 3.3V following SD 3.0 protocol.
Steps.17: Check that SDIO_1_SEL (CH2) switches from LOW to HIGH, the voltage at SD_VCCB (CH1) is 1.8V.
Steps.18: Take an oscilloscope screenshot (with and without zoom).
